title: The film I saw
goal: Tell Sēf about a film you saw, using illi with an ending that points back to the noun
tip: When the noun is the object of the verb after illi, the verb takes an ending that points back to it: il-film illi shiftah 'the film I saw' (lit. that I saw it). Plural things take -ha: il-aghāni illi simaʿt-ha 'the songs I heard', it-tadhākir illi shirēt-ha 'the tickets I bought'.
grammar: resumptive pronoun: il-film illi shiftah 'the film (that) I saw'
dialogue: A
هلا! شو الفلم اللي شفته أمس؟
hala! shu l-film illi shiftah ams?
Hi! What was the film you saw yesterday?
B
فلم يديد. وايد عجبني!
film yidīd. wāyid ʿajabni!
A new film. I really liked it!
A
والممثل اللي تحبه، كان فيه؟
w il-mumaththil illi tḥibbah, kān fīh?
And the actor you like, was he in it?
B
هيه. والأغاني اللي سمعتها حلوة بعد
hē. w il-aghāni illi simaʿt-ha ḥilwa baʿad
Yes. And the songs I heard (in it) are good too.
A
زين، بشوفه. والتذاكر اللي شريتها، غالية؟
zēn, bashūfah. w it-tadhākir illi shirēt-ha, ghālya?
Great, I'll see it. And the tickets you bought, are they expensive?
B
لا، رخيصة. بس الفشار اللي كلته كان غالي!
la, rakhīṣa. bas il-fashār illi kaltah kān ghāli!
No, they're cheap. But the popcorn I ate was expensive!
A
دوم جي! تنصحني أشوفه في السينما؟
dōm chī! tinṣaḥni ashūfah fi s-sīnama?
It's always like that! Would you recommend I see it at the cinema?
B
أكيد، يستاهل. شوفه في السينما، مب في التلفون
akīd, yistāhil. shūfah fi s-sīnama, mub fi t-tilifōn
Definitely, it's worth it. Watch it at the cinema, not on your phone.
items: that I saw; that you saw (to a man)
to a woman: illi shiftīh (اللي شفتيه); about a feminine noun or plural things: illi shift-ha (اللي شفتها)
I liked it (lit. it pleased me)
did you like it?: ʿajabak? (to a woman: ʿajabich?)
the actor you like (to a man)
to a woman: illi tḥibbīnah (اللي تحبينه); actors: il-mumaththilīn (الممثلين)
the songs, the music (in a film)
that I heard (a feminine noun or plural things); that you heard (to a man)
about a masculine noun: illi simaʿtah (اللي سمعته); to a woman: illi simaʿtīha (اللي سمعتيها)
I'll see it, I'll watch it
the tickets I bought; the tickets you bought (to a man)
plural things take -ha; to a woman: illi shirētīha (اللي شريتيها)
would you recommend it? (lit. do you advise me?) (to a man)

title: The place I told you about
goal: Suggest a restaurant to Maryam for the office lunch, with illi and a preposition that points back
tip: After a preposition, the ending that points back goes on the preposition: il-maṭʿam illi gilt-lich ʿannah 'the restaurant I told you about', illi ṭalabna minnah 'the one we ordered from'. English can leave 'about' or 'from' at the end; Gulf Arabic always gives it an ending.
grammar: resumptive pronoun after a preposition: illi gilt-lich ʿannah
dialogue: A
بنطلب غدا للمكتب. تعرف مطعم زين؟
biniṭlub ghada lil-maktab. taʿarf maṭʿam zēn?
We're ordering lunch for the office. Do you know a good restaurant?
B
هيه، المطعم اللي قلت لج عنه. أكله حلو
hē, il-maṭʿam illi gilt-lich ʿannah. aklah ḥilu
Yes, the restaurant I told you about. The food there is good.
A
اللي في البناية اللي يم المترو؟
illi fi l-bināya illi yamm il-mitrō?
The one in the building by the metro?
B
لا، هذاك اللي رحت له ويا الشباب الأسبوع اللي طاف
la, hādhāk illi riḥt-lah wiyya sh-shabāb il-usbūʿ illi ṭāf
No, the one I went to with the guys last week.
A
زين. والمكان اللي تتكلم عنه، غالي؟
zēn. w il-makān illi titkallam ʿannah, ghāli?
OK. And this place you're talking about, is it expensive?
B
لا، رخيص. المطعم اللي طلبنا منه أمس كان أغلى
la, rkhīṣ. il-maṭʿam illi ṭalabna minnah ams kān aghla
No, it's cheap. The one we ordered from yesterday was more expensive.
A
خلاص، نطلب منه. طرش لي الرقم اللي عندك
khalāṣ, niṭlub minnah. ṭarrish-li r-ragam illi ʿindak
Right, we'll order from there. Send me the number you've got.
B
زين، دقيقة وأطرش لج
zēn, dagīga w aṭarrish-lich
OK, give me a minute and I'll send it to you.
items: (the one) I told you about (to a woman)
to a man: illi gilt-lak ʿannah (اللي قلت لك عنه); about a feminine noun: ʿanha
about a feminine noun: illi riḥt-lha (اللي رحت لها)
(the one) you're talking about (to a man)
to a woman: illi titkallamīn ʿannah (اللي تتكلمين عنه)
we ordered from it, we ordered from him
the food's good there (lit. its food is good)
we're going to order, we'll order
the number you've got (to a man)
to a woman: ir-ragam illi ʿindich (الرقم اللي عندج)

title: Whoever wants to come, comes
goal: Plan a desert trip with Sēf and the guys, saying 'whoever…' with illi on its own
tip: illi with no noun before it means 'whoever, anyone who': illi yabi yrūḥ, yrūḥ 'whoever wants to go can go'. Its verb takes the 'he' form (y-), even when it means anyone: illi yitʼakhkhar yghassil il-mawāʿīn 'whoever's late washes the dishes'.
grammar: headless illi 'whoever': illi yabi yrūḥ, yrūḥ
dialogue: B
شباب، يوم السبت بنروح البر. تيون ويانا؟
shabāb, yōm is-sabt binrūḥ il-barr. tiyūn wiyyāna?
Guys, on Saturday we're going to the desert. Are you coming with us?
A
أنا ياي أكيد. بس ما في مكان للكل في سيارتي
ana yāy akīd. bas ma fī makān lil-kill fi sayyārti
I'm coming for sure. But there isn't room for everyone in my car.
B
عادي، اللي عنده سيارة ييبها
ʿādi, illi ʿindah sayyāra yībha
No problem, whoever has a car brings it.
A
زين. واللي ما يقدر ييي؟
zēn. w illi ma yigdar yiyi?
OK. And whoever can't come?
B
براحته. بس اللي يبي ييي، ييي
b-rāḥtah. bas illi yabi yiyi, yiyi
That's up to him. But whoever wants to come, comes.
A
والأكل؟ منو بيسويه؟
w il-akil? minu biysawwīh?
And the food? Who's going to make it?
B
اللي يوصل أول يسوي القهوة، وأنا علي العشا
illi yōṣal awwal ysawwi l-gahwa, w ana ʿalay il-ʿasha
Whoever gets there first makes the coffee, and I'll do dinner.
A
حلو! واللي يتأخر يغسل المواعين
ḥilu! w illi yitʼakhkhar yghassil il-mawāʿīn
Nice! And whoever's late washes the dishes.
items: illi yabi yrūḥ, yrūḥ = whoever wants to go can go; whoever doesn't want: illi ma yabi
whoever has a car, anyone with a car
that's up to him, as he likes
up to you: b-rāḥtak (to a man), b-rāḥtich (to a woman)
I'll wash the dishes: baghassil il-mawāʿīn (بغسل المواعين)
are you coming with us? (to a group)
to one man: tiyi wiyyāna?; to one woman: tiyīn wiyyāna?

title: Whatever you think
goal: Choose a present for your dad with Sēf, using illi for 'what, whatever'
tip: illi on its own also means 'what, whatever'. Like a noun, it takes the ending that points back: illi tshūfah 'whatever you think (best)', khudh illi tigdar ʿalēh 'get what you can afford'. With no verb: illi maʿi 'what I've got on me'.
grammar: headless illi 'what, whatever': illi tshūfah, illi tishtirīh
dialogue: B
أبي أشتري هدية حق أبوي. شو أشتري له؟
abi ashtiri hadiyya ḥagg ubūy. shu ashtirī-lah?
I want to buy a present for my dad. What should I get him?
A
اللي يحبه هو. شو يحب؟
illi yḥibbah huwa. shu yḥibb?
Whatever he likes. What does he like?
B
ما أدري! دوم يقول: اللي تشتريه زين
ma adri! dōm ygūl: illi tishtirīh zēn
I don't know! He always says: whatever you buy is fine.
A
عيل خذ له دلة. يحب القهوة العربية؟
ʿayal khudh-lah dalla. yḥibb il-gahwa l-ʿarabiyya?
Then get him a dalla. Does he like Arabic coffee?
B
هيه، وايد! بس اختار لي انت، اللي تشوفه
hē, wāyid! bas ikhtār-li inta, illi tshūfah
Yes, a lot! But you choose for me, whatever you think.
A
هذي. بس شوف السعر قبل لا تدفع!
hādhi. bas shūf is-siʿir gabil la tidfaʿ!
This one. But check the price before you pay!
B
لا! اللي معي ما يكفي
la! illi maʿi ma ykaffi
Oh no! What I've got on me isn't enough.
A
عادي، خذ اللي تقدر عليه. هذي الصغيرة أرخص
ʿādi, khudh illi tigdar ʿalēh. hādhi ṣ-ṣghīra arkhaṣ
Never mind, get what you can afford. This small one's cheaper.
items: whatever you think (best), as you see fit (to a man)
to a woman: illi tshūfīnah (اللي تشوفينه)
whatever he likes; (the one) he likes
about a woman: illi tḥibbah (اللي تحبه)
to a woman: illi tishtirīnah (اللي تشترينه)
get him, buy him (to a man)
what you can afford, what you can manage (to a man)
to a woman: illi tigdarīn ʿalēh (اللي تقدرين عليه)

title: The file? I haven't opened it
goal: Catch up with Maryam at the office, putting the topic first: il-mudīr, ma shiftah
tip: Gulf speakers often name the thing first, then comment on it with an ending that points back: il-mudīr, ma shiftah il-yōm 'the manager, I haven't seen him today'; il-īmēlāt, garēt-ha killha 'the emails, I've read them all'. Plural things take -ha.
grammar: topic first with a pointing-back ending: il-mudīr, ma shiftah il-yōm
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. المدير، شفته اليوم؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. il-mudīr, shiftah il-yōm?
Good morning. Have you seen the manager today?
B
صباح النور. لا، المدير ما شفته اليوم. يمكن عنده اجتماع
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. la, il-mudīr ma shiftah il-yōm. yimkin ʿindah ijtimāʿ
Good morning. No, I haven't seen the manager today. Maybe he's got a meeting.
A
والإيميلات اللي طرشتها أمس، قريتها؟
w il-īmēlāt illi ṭarrasht-ha ams, garēt-ha?
And the emails I sent yesterday, have you read them?
B
هيه، الإيميلات قريتها كلها. بس الملف ما فتحته
hē, il-īmēlāt garēt-ha killha. bas il-malaff ma fataḥtah
Yes, I've read all the emails. But I haven't opened the file.
A
الملف لازم تشوفه قبل الاجتماع
il-malaff lāzim tshūfah gabil il-ijtimāʿ
You need to look at the file before the meeting.
B
إن شاء الله. والأرقام اللي فيه، منو بيشوفها؟
in shāʼ allāh. w il-argām illi fīh, minu biyshūfha?
Will do. And the figures in it, who's going to check them?
A
الأرقام انت تشوفها، والعرض أنا سويته
il-argām inta tshūfha, w il-ʿarẓ ana sawwētah
You check the figures, and I've done the presentation.
B
زين. بس المدير، لا تقولين له إني ما فتحته!
zēn. bas il-mudīr, la tgūlīn-lah inni ma fataḥtah!
OK. But don't tell the manager I haven't opened it!
items: about a woman: ma shift-ha l-yōm (ما شفتها اليوم)
I've read them all, I read all of it
about a masculine noun: garētah killah (قريته كله)
I haven't opened it, I didn't open it
you need to look at it (to a man)
to a woman: lāzim tshūfīnah (لازم تشوفينه)
who's going to look at them? who'll check it? (a feminine noun or plural things)
about a masculine noun: minu biyshūfah? (منو بيشوفه؟)
you look at them, you check them (to a man)
to a woman: inti tshūfīnha (انتي تشوفينها)
I've done it, I did it (myself)
about a feminine noun: ana sawwēt-ha (أنا سويتها)
to a man: la tgūl-lah (لا تقول له)

title: Happy Ramadan
goal: Greet Sēf at the start of Ramadan and accept an invitation to iftar at Bū Rāshid's
tip: At the start of Ramadan say shahrak mubārak to a man (shahrich mubārak to a woman); the reply is allāh ybārik fīk. Invitations often use a participle: ʿammi ʿāzmak ʿala l-fuṭūr 'my uncle's invited you to iftar'. Plans take b-: basāʿid 'I'll help'.
grammar: recycle: participles (ʿāzmak) and the b- future in plans
dialogue: A
هلا سالم! شهرك مبارك
hala Sālim! shahrak mubārak
Hi Sālim! Happy Ramadan.
B
الله يبارك فيك. أول يوم في رمضان، الحمد لله
allāh ybārik fīk. awwal yōm fi ramaẓān, il-ḥamdu lillāh
Thank you (lit. God bless you). The first day of Ramadan, thank God.
A
عمي بو راشد عازمك على الفطور يوم الخميس
ʿammi Bū Rāshid ʿāzmak ʿala l-fuṭūr yōm il-khamīs
My uncle Bū Rāshid's invited you to iftar on Thursday.
B
ما قصر! على هالخشم. متى أوصل؟
ma gaṣṣar! ʿala hal-khashim. mita ōṣal?
That's so kind of him! I'd love to. When should I get there?
A
قبل الأذان بشوي. واللي يوصل بدري يساعد!
gabil il-adhān b-shwayy. w illi yōṣal badri ysāʿid!
A little before the call to prayer. And whoever gets there early helps out!
B
أكيد بساعد. أييب شي وياي؟
akīd basāʿid. ayīb shay wiyyāy?
Of course I'll help. Shall I bring anything?
A
لا، مب لازم تييب شي. وبالليل نصلي التراويح ويا عمي
la, mub lāzim tyīb shay. w bil-lēl nṣalli t-tarāwīḥ wiyya ʿammi
No, you don't need to bring anything. And at night we pray tarawih with my uncle.
B
إن شاء الله. الله يخليه
in shāʼ allāh. allāh ykhallīh
God willing. Bless him.
items: happy Ramadan (lit. blessed be your month) (to a man)
to a woman: shahrich mubārak (شهرج مبارك); the reply is allāh ybārik fīk (to a woman: fīch)
(he's) invited you to iftar (to a man)
that's so kind of him (lit. he didn't fall short)
tarawih, the night prayers of Ramadan
bless him (warm thanks for someone's kindness; lit. God keep him)
culture: On the first night of Ramadan, the family usually gathers for iftar at the house of the head of the family, often the grandfather. Two weeks before Ramadan, on the night of 15 Shaʿbān, Emirati children celebrate ḥagg il-lēla: after maghrib they go from house to house in traditional clothes, carrying woven bags and singing, and neighbours give them sweets and nuts.

title: Iftar at the majlis
goal: Break the fast at Bū Rāshid's majlis with the right greetings and replies
tip: Each greeting has its reply: ramaẓān karīm → allāhu akram; ḥayyāk allāh → allāh yḥayyīk; mā gaṣṣart → mā sawwēna shay; tagabbal allāh → minna w minkum. Say bismillāh before the first date. illi again: il-harīs illi tḥibbah 'the harees you like'.
grammar: recycle: illi and the Ramadan replies
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. رمضان كريم يا عمي!
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. ramaẓān karīm yā ʿammi!
Peace be upon you. Ramadan Kareem, uncle!
A
وعليكم السلام. الله أكرم! حياك الله يا سالم
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. allāhu akram! ḥayyāk allāh yā Sālim
And peace be upon you. God is more generous! Welcome, Sālim.
B
الله يحييك يا طويل العمر. ما شاء الله، كل هذا أكل!
allāh yḥayyīk yā ṭawīl il-ʿumr. mā shāʼ allāh, kill hādha akil!
Thank you, sir. Wow, all this food!
A
كله من البيت. هذا الثريد، والهريس اللي تحبه
killah min il-bēt. hādha th-tharīd, w il-harīs illi tḥibbah
It's all home-made. This is thareed, and (here's) the harees you like.
B
الله يخليك، ما قصرت
allāh ykhallīk, mā gaṣṣart
Thank you so much, you're very kind.
A
ما سوينا شي. يلا، أذن المغرب! خذ تمرة ولبن
mā sawwēna shay. yalla, adhdhan il-maghrib! khudh tamra w laban
It's nothing. Right, there's the maghrib call! Have a date and some laban.
B
بسم الله. تقبل الله يا عمي
bismillāh. tagabbal allāh yā ʿammi
In the name of God. May God accept (our fast), uncle.
A
منا ومنكم. نصلي المغرب، وبعدين ناكل
minna w minkum. nṣalli l-maghrib, w baʿdēn nākil
From us and from you. We'll pray maghrib, and then we'll eat.
items: it's all home-made (lit. all of it is from the house)
thareed (bread soaked in a meat and vegetable stew)
in the name of God (before eating or starting something)
the harees you like (to a man)
to a woman: illi tḥibbīnah (اللي تحبينه)
we pray maghrib; we'll pray maghrib
culture: The fast is broken with dates and laban (buttermilk), and harees and thareed are common iftar dishes. Later in the evening, after the ʿishāʼ prayer, come the tarawih prayers, every night of Ramadan.

title: Eid morning
goal: Wish Sēf a happy Eid after the Eid prayer and plan a visit to his family
tip: To ʿīdak mubārak 'happy Eid' (to a man) the reply is min il-ʿāydīn wil-fāyzīn. ʿasākum min ʿuwwādah is answered with the same words. Participles again: ummi msawwya ghada 'my mum's made lunch'.
grammar: recycle: participles (msawwya) and the b- future
dialogue: A
عيدك مبارك يا سالم!
ʿīdak mubārak yā Sālim!
Happy Eid, Sālim!
B
من العايدين والفايزين! عساكم من عواده
min il-ʿāydīn wil-fāyzīn! ʿasākum min ʿuwwādah
And to you (lit. may you be among those who return and win)! Happy Eid to you all.
A
عساكم من عواده. صليت العيد؟
ʿasākum min ʿuwwādah. ṣallēt il-ʿīd?
Happy Eid to you too. Did you go to the Eid prayer?
B
هيه، في المسجد اللي يم شقتي. كان زحمة!
hē, fi l-masjid illi yamm shiggti. kān zaḥma!
Yes, at the mosque near my flat. It was packed!
A
تعال البيت، الأهل كلهم هناك. أمي مسوية غدا
taʿāl il-bēt, il-ahal killhum hnāk. ummi msawwya ghada
Come over to ours, the whole family's there. My mum's made lunch.
B
إن شاء الله. وعيال عمك، أعطيهم عيدية؟
in shāʼ allāh. w ʿyāl ʿammak, aʿṭīhum ʿīdiyya?
Sure. And your cousins, should I give them Eid money?
A
إذا تبي، بس مب لازم. أكيد بيستانسون!
idha tabi, bas mub lāzim. akīd biyistānsūn!
If you like, but you don't have to. They'll love it, for sure!
B
زين، بعطي كل واحد عشرين درهم
zēn, baʿṭi kill wāḥid ʿishrīn dirham
OK, I'll give each of them twenty dirhams.
items: to a woman: ʿīdich mubārak; to a group: ʿīdkum mubārak; the reply is min il-ʿāydīn wil-fāyzīn
and to you (the reply to ʿīdak mubārak; lit. among those who return and win)
also said on its own as an Eid wish
did you go to the Eid prayer? (to a man)
to a woman: ṣallēti l-ʿīd? (صليتي العيد؟)
I give them; shall I give them?
they'll love it, they'll be happy
come over (to our house) (to a man)
to a woman: taʿāli l-bēt (تعالي البيت)
culture: Eid al-Fitr starts with the Eid prayer, usually shortly after sunrise. Families then have breakfast together and go round visiting relatives and friends, where guests get Arabic coffee and dates and sweets such as luqaimat. Many people wear something new, and children get ʿīdiyya, a little money from parents, grandparents and older relatives.

title: Friday prayer
goal: Arrange to go to the Friday prayer with Sēf and ask about the time and the sermon
tip: Friday plans use the b- future: bitṣalli wiyyāna? 'will you pray with us?', batsabbaḥ 'I'll have a shower', bakūn ʿindak 'I'll be at yours'. Headless illi again: illi yiyi mitʼakhkhir tfūtah il-khuṭba 'whoever comes late misses the sermon'.
grammar: recycle: the b- future and headless illi
dialogue: A
اليوم الجمعة. بتصلي ويانا في المسجد الكبير؟
il-yōm il-jumʿa. bitṣalli wiyyāna fi l-masjid il-kbīr?
It's Friday today. Will you pray with us at the big mosque?
B
أكيد. صلاة الجمعة الساعة كم الحين؟
akīd. ṣalāt il-jumʿa s-sāʿa cham il-ḥīn?
Definitely. What time is the Friday prayer these days?
A
وحدة إلا ربع، في كل الإمارات. غيروا الوقت
waḥda illa rubʿ, fi kill il-Imārāt. ghayyaraw il-wagt
Quarter to one, all over the Emirates. They changed the time.
B
زين. والخطبة قبل الصلاة، صح؟
zēn. w il-khuṭba gabil iṣ-ṣalā, ṣaḥḥ?
OK. And the sermon's before the prayer, right?
A
هيه. واللي ييي متأخر تفوته الخطبة
hē. w illi yiyi mitʼakhkhir tfūtah il-khuṭba
Yes. And whoever comes late misses the sermon.
B
عيل بتسبح وبلبس، وبكون عندك الساعة ثنعش
ʿayal batsabbaḥ w balbas, w bakūn ʿindak is-sāʿa thnaʿash
Then I'll have a shower and get dressed, and I'll be at yours at twelve.
A
زين. ولا تنسى، التلفون على الصامت وقت الخطبة
zēn. w la tinsa, it-tilifōn ʿala ṣ-ṣāmit wagt il-khuṭba
OK. And don't forget: phone on silent during the sermon.
B
أكيد. وبعد الصلاة، الغدا علي
akīd. w baʿd iṣ-ṣalā, il-ghada ʿalay
Sure. And after the prayer, lunch is on me.
items: the same letters also spell il-khiṭba 'the engagement'
will you pray with us? (to a man)
to a woman: bitṣallīn wiyyāna? (بتصلين ويانا؟)
I'll be at yours, I'll be at your place (to a man)
to a woman: bakūn ʿindich (بكون عندج)
culture: Since January 2026 the Friday sermon and prayer start at 12:45 pm in every mosque in the UAE; from 2022 they started at 1:15 pm. The UAE weekend is Saturday and Sunday, so Friday is a working day for many people. The sermon comes first, and worshippers are urged to arrive early so they don't miss it.

title: Sad news
goal: Offer Sēf your condolences when his father's uncle dies, and ask about the ʿazā
tip: When you hear of a death, say allāh yirḥamah 'God have mercy on him' (the reply is āmīn), and to the family ʿaẓẓam allāh ajrakum; they answer ajrana w ajrakum. Reported speech again: simaʿt inn ʿamm ubūk twaffa 'I heard your dad's uncle passed away'.
grammar: recycle: reported speech (simaʿt inn) and kān + adjective
dialogue: B
سيف، سمعت إن عم أبوك توفى. الله يرحمه
Sēf, simaʿt inn ʿamm ubūk twaffa. allāh yirḥamah
Sēf, I heard your dad's uncle passed away. God have mercy on him.
A
آمين. هيه، البارحة بالليل. كان مريض من زمان
āmīn. hē, il-bārḥa bil-lēl. kān marīẓ min zamān
Amen. Yes, last night. He'd been ill for a long time.
B
إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون. عظم الله أجركم
innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn. ʿaẓẓam allāh ajrakum
We belong to God and to Him we return. May God reward you all (in your loss).
A
أجرنا وأجركم. الله يخليك يا سالم
ajrana w ajrakum. allāh ykhallīk yā Sālim
And you too. Thank you, Sālim.
B
وين العزا؟ ودي أييكم
wēn il-ʿazā? widdi ayīkum
Where's the ʿazā? I'd like to come and see you.
A
في بيتهم في الشارقة، ثلاث أيام بالليل
fi bēt-hum fi sh-Shārja, thalāth ayyām bil-lēl
At their house in Sharjah, for three days, in the evenings.
B
إن شاء الله بيي الليلة. الله يصبركم
in shāʼ allāh bayi l-lēla. allāh yṣabbirkum
I'll come tonight, God willing. May God give you all patience.
A
آمين يا رب. نشوفك الليلة
āmīn yā rabb. nshūfak il-lēla
Amen. See you tonight.
items: God have mercy on him (said whenever you mention someone who has died)
about a woman: allāh yirḥamha (الله يرحمها); the reply is āmīn
my condolences (to the family; lit. may God make your reward great)
to one man: ʿaẓẓam allāh ajrak; to one woman: ʿaẓẓam allāh ajrich; the reply is ajrana w ajrakum
and you too (the reply to ʿaẓẓam allāh ajrakum; lit. our reward and yours)
to one man: ajrana w ajrak (أجرنا وأجرك); to one woman: ajrana w ajrich (أجرنا وأجرج)
innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn
we belong to God and to Him we return (said on hearing of a death)
she passed away: twaffat (توفت); the plain word for 'died' is māt (مات)
he'd been ill for a long time
the ʿazā (where the family receive condolences)
to one man: allāh yṣabbrak (الله يصبرك); to one woman: allāh yṣabbrich; the reply is āmīn
I'd like to come and see you (all)

title: At the ʿazā
goal: Give your condolences to Bū Rāshid at the family's ʿazā, sit a while and take your leave
tip: At the ʿazā, say ʿaẓẓam allāh ajrakum to the family. As you leave they may say maʼjūr 'God reward you (for coming)'; answer w iyyāk 'and you too'. kān + a present verb means 'used to': kān ysāʿid il-kill 'he used to help everyone'.
grammar: recycle: kān + present verb 'used to', reported speech, headless illi
dialogue: B
عظم الله أجركم يا عمي
ʿaẓẓam allāh ajrakum yā ʿammi
May God reward you all (in your loss), uncle.
A
أجرنا وأجركم. حياك الله يا ولدي، تفضل اقعد
ajrana w ajrakum. ḥayyāk allāh yā wildi, tfaẓẓal igʿid
And you too. Welcome, son, please sit down.
B
الله يحييك. الله يرحمه، سيف قال لي إنه كان يساعد الكل
allāh yḥayyīk. allāh yirḥamah, Sēf gāl-li innah kān ysāʿid il-kill
Thank you. God have mercy on him. Sēf told me he used to help everyone.
A
آمين. هيه والله، اللي يعرفه ما ينساه
āmīn. hē wallāh, illi yaʿarfah ma yinsāh
Amen. Yes, truly. Anyone who knows him never forgets him.
B
عن إذنك يا عمي، لازم أمشي. الله يصبركم
ʿan idhnak yā ʿammi, lāzim amshi. allāh yṣabbirkum
Excuse me, uncle, I have to go. May God give you all patience.
A
آمين. مأجور يا ولدي، الله يحفظك
āmīn. maʼjūr yā wildi, allāh yiḥfaẓak
Amen. God reward you (for coming), son. God keep you.
B
وإياك يا عمي
w iyyāk yā ʿammi
And you too, uncle.
items: God reward you (to someone who has done a good deed, e.g. come to an ʿazā)
to a woman: maʼjūra (مأجورة); to a group: maʼjūrīn (مأجورين); the reply is w iyyāk
and you too (the reply to maʼjūr and other blessings) (to a man)
to a woman: w iyyāch (وإياج); to a group: w iyyākum (وإياكم)
to a woman: tfaẓẓali igʿidi (تفضلي اقعدي)
she used to help: kānat tsāʿid (كانت تساعد)
anyone who knows him never forgets him
I have to go, I must be off
God keep you (a warm goodbye or thanks) (to a man)
to a woman: allāh yiḥfaẓich (الله يحفظج)
culture: An Emirati ʿazā lasts up to three days after the burial, often in a majlis at the family home, and women mourners sit separately. A man says as-salāmu ʿalaykum as he comes in, shakes hands with everyone seated, says ʿaẓẓam allāh ajrak to the relatives and sits for a while. Talk stays quiet and respectful, and the dead are spoken of well.
